label: 1-second
definition: A temporal resolution of one value per second.
comment: It is typical of raw anemometer sampling and is used to study turbulence and gusts.

label: 1-minute
definition: A temporal resolution of one value per minute.
comment: It is common for automatic weather stations and for solar radiation measurements that resolve passing clouds.

label: 2-minute
definition: A temporal resolution of one value per two-minute interval.
comment: It is used by some automatic weather stations, notably for wind averages at airports.

label: 5-minute
definition: A temporal resolution of one value per five-minute interval.
comment: It is common in power system operation and in high-frequency solar and wind records.

label: 10-minute
definition: A temporal resolution of one value per ten-minute interval.
comment: Ten-minute averages are the standard for wind measurements at met masts and in the IEC 61400 wind turbine standards.

label: 15-minute
definition: A temporal resolution of one value per fifteen-minute interval.
comment: It is common for electricity metering, power output records and some satellite irradiance products.

label: 30-minute
definition: A temporal resolution of one value per thirty-minute interval.
comment: It is common in some meteorological networks and satellite radiation products.

label: hourly
definition: A temporal resolution of one value per hour.
comment: Hourly values resolve the daily cycle and are common in station records and reanalysis data such as ERA5.

label: 3-hourly
definition: A temporal resolution of one value every three hours.
comment: It is common for synoptic weather observations and for some reanalysis and satellite products.

label: 6-hourly
definition: A temporal resolution of one value every six hours.
comment: It is typical of older reanalysis products and of the main synoptic hours (00, 06, 12 and 18 UTC).

label: daily
definition: A temporal resolution of one value per day.
comment: Daily values are common for precipitation, river discharge and solar irradiation. They smooth out the daily cycle.

label: monthly
definition: A temporal resolution of one value per month.
comment: Monthly values describe the seasonal variation of a resource, such as monthly mean wind speeds or discharges.

label: seasonal
definition: A temporal resolution of one value per season.
comment: Seasons may be meteorological, such as December–February (DJF), or regional, such as rainy and dry seasons.

label: annual
definition: A temporal resolution of one value per year.
comment: Annual values, such as the annual mean wind speed or annual energy production, hide seasonal variation.

label: long-term
definition: A single value aggregated over the whole period of record.
comment: A long-term mean summarizes a resource over several years and is the usual reference for estimating the expected energy yield of a site.
